person_note: The novel deliberately alternates sustained narrative persons: Cherry narrates her own history in first person, while the flight passengers and their aftermath are narrated in close third person. Numerous quote passages independently expose Cherry's participating I/we narration, while several sustained present-tense passages expose close-third access to Paula, Eve, Allegra, and other passengers. Generic second-person aphorisms are reader-directed or universal and do not form a second-person strand; dialogue and external epigraphs are non-base material. The authorized Penguin sample directly displays both first- and third-person chapters, and Pan Macmillan's whole-book reading notes explicitly confirm the structure, leaving no material unresolved conflict.
